title: Steve Jobs at D1 (2003): the digital hub, the iTunes Music Store, and why Apple skips tablets and PDAs
summary: At the D1 conference in 2003, Jobs explains the personal computer as the "digital hub", demos the new iTunes Music Store, and says why Apple passes on tablets, PDAs and phones. He also covers how tech and content cultures misunderstand each other, and the hardest part of turning Apple around: laying people off.

principles.text: Own the whole stack so the experience works end to end.
principles.quote: we could do the whole thing. You know, we made the operating system. We could write the applications. We made the computers. We made the iPod. And and we could we could control the whole thing.

principles.text: Bet on real, proven markets rather than speculative ones.
principles.quote: This is not a speculative market. It's a real, tangible market. And um I think if we can bring some value to that market, uh then we'll succeed.

principles.text: Choose where to put resources: build the product, not the broad category.
principles.quote: We chose instead to do the iPod instead of a PDA. That was our that we put our resources behind that.

principles.text: Technology and creative industries must respect each other's craft; creative work is as disciplined as engineering.
principles.quote: The folks on the creative side work as hard as any technology folks I've ever seen in my life. They're just as disciplined.

principles.text: Compete with the real alternative by giving users a compelling, legal option, and assume most people want to be honest.
principles.quote: We're we believe that 80% of the people stealing music don't really want to steal music. We think they'd rather be legal if somebody offered them a competitive, compelling way to be legal.

principles.text: Making hard people decisions is the toughest part of leadership; fix management early and then innovate through downturns.
principles.quote: always the hardest decision I think anybody leading an organization makes is to let people go.
